Kestrel was Theo Kanda's proposal for an internal CRM experiment — a
lightweight tracker for studio client relationships — announced at the March
all-hands (m-004). Kestrel started 2026-03-31, the day after the all-hands;
Theo prototyped contact pages and Lorna Vey ran a two-week ops trial.

Cancelled 2026-04-21 (decision d-010): with the ops trial load falling on
Lorna alone, no one could own it. Data export and teardown happened in s-009.

March all-hands. Status: Ledgerline invoicing live with flat monthly runs,
Wayfare in the field across the pilot stations, Larkspur Archive scanning
and OCR underway. New: Theo proposed the Kestrel CRM experiment — a
lightweight internal client tracker — and got a two-week trial window; the
Beacon Grid engagement with Greenline Utilities starts next week on the
Northpost feeds. Capacity: everyone heads down until Wayfare ships.

Context: Kestrel has run as a two-week ops trial on top of Lorna's existing
load; Theo's prototype works, but no one can own the tool going forward.

Options considered: keep it as a side project; adopt it with an owner; cancel.

Decision: cancel the Kestrel CRM experiment, agreed at the go/no-go (m-006)
— the studio's client count does not justify the maintenance surface. Export
the trial data and tear down (s-009).

Consequences: client tracking stays in Ledgerline notes; Theo returns fully
to Wayfare and Beacon Grid.

Go/no-go on Kestrel after the two-week trial: Theo's prototype works, but
the ops load fell on Lorna alone and no one can own the tool going forward —
the studio's client count does not justify the maintenance surface. No-go;
d-010 cancelled the experiment the next day, with data export and teardown
in s-009.

final_answer:
The cancellation of the Kestrel CRM experiment was influenced by **two key factors**:

1. **Operational burden fell solely on Lorna Vey** — The two-week ops trial load landed entirely on Lorna with no one else able to own the tool going forward. As recorded in the go/no-go meeting (m-006): "the ops load fell on Lorna alone and no one can own the tool going forward."

2. **Insufficient client volume to justify maintenance** — The studio's client count did not justify the maintenance surface required for the CRM. Decision d-010 states: "the studio's client count does not justify the maintenance surface."

These factors were discussed at the Kestrel go/no-go meeting (m-006) on 2026-04-20, leading to the cancellation decision (d-010) the next day, with data export and teardown completed in session s-009.
